roles.name: control
roles.appliesTo: Buttons, inputs, nav items, badges, and small tiles nested inside a card.

roles.name: card
roles.appliesTo: Cards, panels, figures, form containers, popovers.

roles.name: frame
roles.appliesTo: Dark media chrome and large full-bleed feature panels.

derived.--radius-frame-inner: calc(var(--radius-frame) - var(--radius-frame-inset)) = 12px. Concentric inner corner for a screen inset inside a padded frame.

exceptions.--radius-arch: 13.75rem. The arch silhouette behind portrait CTAs — a shape, not a radius role. Its base corners still use the frame role.
exceptions.pill: 999px, reserved for compact labels, categories, and capsule controls.

radiusMeta.note: Images carry no radius; the container that clips them owns the corner.

roles.name: focus-ring
roles.appliesTo: Anything with its own box: buttons, inputs, nav items, cards, media posters, icon buttons.
roles.contrast: ~4.6:1 accent on cream — clears the 3:1 non-text floor.

roles.name: focus-ring-on-dark
roles.appliesTo: The same, on a navy section where the accent would disappear. The wider gap keeps the warm ring from fusing with the dark backdrop.

roles.name: focus-underline
roles.appliesTo: Inline text links that can wrap. An outline follows the text across a line break; a ring would draw one rectangle around the whole line box.

mechanism.trigger: :focus-visible only, never :focus — a plain :focus fires on mouse click and shows the indicator to people who did not ask for it.
mechanism.layer: Rules live in @layer focus, which Tailwind never declares. An undeclared layer sorts after every declared one, so the ring outranks any hover:shadow-* utility regardless of source order. This is also why they are plain classes rather than @utility.
mechanism.--focus-ring-keep: box-shadow replaces rather than stacks. An element whose drop shadow should survive while focused hands it to this custom property, which the ring appends to its own shadow list.

exceptions.radix-menus: Radix-driven menus keep focus:bg-accent for their roving highlight. That is a selection affordance the library manages by keyboard, not a focus indicator, so it sits outside these roles.

focusMeta.note: The ring is never faded. The 20-40% opacity variants this system replaced measured about 1.9:1, below the 3:1 non-text contrast floor.

motionMeta.easeNote: One decelerating curve for everything. Motion that decelerates arrives settled instead of stopping dead. Nothing eases in — an element that starts slowly feels unresponsive to the click that triggered it.
motionMeta.scale: Speed follows travel distance, not importance. The further a thing moves, the longer it needs to stay believable.
motionMeta.split: The roles set duration and easing only, for animations as well as transitions. The call site declares what animates because the property list is a per-component decision and the speed is a system one. Explicit property lists name translate or scale, not transform, because Tailwind v4 compiles movement to standalone properties.

entrance.why: The one speed outside the scale. A scroll-in entrance reads as sluggish below 700ms; it is content arriving, not an interaction responding.

reducedMotion.why: A blanket guard rather than per-component motion-reduce: variants. Honouring the preference only where a developer remembered to opt in means it gets missed, and the misses are invisible to anyone not testing with the setting on.
reducedMotion.transitions: Collapse to 1ms, not 0, so transitionend still fires and any JS waiting on it does not hang.
reducedMotion.travel: Hover lifts and scale echoes are zeroed by naming the movement utilities individually. Tailwind v4 drives them through standalone translate and scale properties, so the guard resets --tw-translate-* and --tw-scale-*. A blanket reset would also erase static positioning such as -translate-x-1/2 and relocate centered UI.
reducedMotion.kept: Opacity and colour still change. A cross-fade carries no travel and is what most reduced-motion users expect to keep.

exceptions.transition-all: Banned. It animates properties nobody intended, including layout ones, and is the usual cause of a mysteriously janky hover.
exceptions.transform: Left untouched by the reduced-motion guard. The theme toggle rotates its sun/moon icons through it, and that is a state indicator rather than decorative travel.

scale.name: size-4
scale.purpose: The default: inside buttons, links, list items.

iconMeta.buttonDefault: size-4 is applied automatically by the button's [&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4. An icon inside a button needs no size class at all.

exceptions.circular-containers: size-10 / size-[46px] / size-16 are surfaces, not icons — a filled disc holding an icon. They follow the shape and spacing scales; the icon inside them still comes from the scale above.
exceptions.play-discs: size-[76px] and md:size-[5.5rem] on media posters are scaled to the poster rather than to a UI scale — single-purpose decorative affordances, sized by composition.

borderMeta.widthNote: One width for the whole system. Emphasis comes from colour, never from thickness.

roles.name: border-border
roles.purpose: The default: cards, panels, dividers, table rules.

roles.name: border-border-strong
roles.purpose: Emphasis: outline controls that must hold their own beside a solid button.

roles.name: border-input
roles.purpose: Form fields at rest, before focus takes over.

roles.name: border-edge-on-dark
roles.purpose: Structural edges on always-navy sections: media frames, dividers.

roles.name: border-edge-on-dark-strong
roles.purpose: Controls sitting on a navy surface.

rejected.why: Used at four call sites to signal emphasis. At devicePixelRatio 1 the browser rounds it down and it computes to exactly 1px — identical to the default — so the emphasis appeared only on retina screens and the same component read as two different weights depending on the monitor. Verified in the browser, not assumed. Colour-based emphasis renders the same everywhere.

exceptions.css-triangles: Play buttons on media posters use border-y-[11px] / border-l-[18px] on an h-0 w-0 element. That is the CSS triangle trick — borders constructing an arrow shape, not edges. The values are geometry scaled to their disc; tokenizing them as border widths would be a category error.

borderMeta.onDarkNote: Navy sections are always dark regardless of the light/dark theme, so they cannot use --border, which follows the theme switch. These two mirror the light pair the same way focus-ring-on-dark mirrors focus-ring. Named edge- rather than border-border-on-dark to avoid a doubled prefix that reads as a typo.

blockquoteAccent.why: An accent, not an edge, which is why it is a named role rather than a border colour token. Previously three live components disagreed: rich-text-content used border-l-4 + border-accent + a tinted background, story-feature border-l-[3px] + copper, editorial-chapter border-l-[3px] + primary. Now one rule. Size and padding stay with the call site; the mark identifying it as a quote does not vary.

narrative.overview:
PHX Home Loan should feel like a knowledgeable local advisor sitting beside a customer: warm, personal, credible, clear, calm, and locally grounded. The system earns trust through legible explanations, real people, useful evidence, and confident next steps. It does not borrow authority from cold institutional banking or luxury-mortgage gloss.

The canonical implementation and shared tokens are the design authority. Prototypes in `PHXHomeLoan-web-prototype` express the intended composition and editorial direction, with one correction: their exported copper accents should usually be Advisor Teal. Legacy and template blocks are anti-reference; their generic colors, typography, and component language must not be propagated into new canonical work.
keyCharacteristics: Warm editorial typography paired with plainspoken interface copy
Advisor Teal actions against navy, paper, ivory, and white surfaces
Restrained Mesa Copper details that add warmth without competing with teal
Structured grids, generous reading space, and evidence-led compositions
Soft, precise geometry with restrained ambient depth
Full WCAG 2.2 AA behavior across states, themes, and viewport sizes

rules.name: The Teal Leads Rule
rules.body: Advisor Teal owns primary actions and active states. Mesa Copper may warm a composition and style subordinate media or editorial actions, but it must never create a second primary action hierarchy.

rules.name: The Explicit Neutral Surface Rule
rules.body: Page Builder sections that expose the Sanity background toggle use white by default and may be set to cream. Reordering sections must not change their surfaces. Sections with designed fixed backgrounds do not expose the toggle.

rules.name: The Editorial Clarity Rule
rules.body: Serif type establishes trust and hierarchy; Archivo carries every task, explanation, label, and action. Do not use the display face as decorative body copy.

rules.name: The One Recipe Rule
rules.body: Components serving the same semantic role share the same complete `typo-*` recipe — size, responsive behavior, weight, line height, and tracking. New typography variants require a new documented role, not an inline override.

rules.name: The One Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Section vertical padding is one of exactly three roles — standard, showpiece, banner. A section that seems to need a fourth value is either mis-tiered or a documented exception.

rules.name: The One Gutter Rule
rules.body: All two-column feature splits share `gap-split`. Widening or narrowing a single section's split is drift, not composition.

rules.name: The Ambient, Not Floating Rule
rules.body: Depth should feel like soft environmental light. Use tonal separation and borders first; reserve stronger shadows for state, overlap, or high-value emphasis.

rules.name: The Softness Has Scale Rule
rules.body: Radius grows with the physical and visual size of the object. Do not apply one exaggerated radius to controls, cards, sections, and media indiscriminately.

rules.name: The Five Shadows Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in the system is one of the five named tokens above, a documented exception, or a `:hover` intensification of one. A new `shadow-[...]` arbitrary value is drift, not composition.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: A button is default or compact. If a design seems to need a different height, the surrounding spacing is usually wrong, not the button — the one exception is a hero action, below.

rules.name: The Earned Shadow Rule
rules.body: Buttons are flat at rest. A resting shadow is an explicit emphasis opt-in, never a default, and never more than one per screen.

rules.name: The Three Corners Rule
rules.body: A corner is control, card, or frame. If a design seems to need a fourth value, it is a container that has not decided which of the three it is.

rules.name: The Concentric Inset Rule
rules.body: When one rounded box sits inside another, the inner radius is the outer radius minus the gap between them. Corners that are not concentric read as a bulge, however small the difference.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: A focusable element wears one of the three focus roles and nothing else. A component that appears to need a custom ring is a component on a surface the system has not yet named.

rules.name: The Ring Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: The focus ring is an accessibility affordance before it is a visual one. It is never faded, never softened to fit a composition, and never removed to tidy up a hover state.

rules.name: The Indicator Follows the Shape Rule
rules.body: Boxes get rings; wrapping text gets outlines. Match the indicator to what the element actually is, not to whichever mechanism the surrounding component happened to use.

rules.name: The Distance Sets the Duration Rule
rules.body: Pick a speed by how far the element travels, not by how important it is. A prominent button that moves 2px still uses `motion-base`; a modest drawer that crosses the screen still uses `motion-slow`.

rules.name: The One Curve Rule
rules.body: Everything decelerates on the same ease-out. A component that appears to need its own curve is nearly always a component that needs a different duration.

rules.name: The Opt-Out Is Not Optional Rule
rules.body: Reduced motion is handled globally, so new components inherit it. Never re-add movement in a way the guard cannot reach — if a new pattern needs a bespoke transform, it belongs in the guard too.

rules.name: The Three Sizes Rule
rules.body: An icon is `size-3.5`, `size-4`, or `size-5`. A value between them is drift — `17px` and `18px` are both a `size-4` that someone nudged.

rules.name: The Icon Follows the Text Rule
rules.body: An icon beside a label matches that label's optical weight rather than being sized independently. When in doubt inside a control, add no size class and inherit the button default.

rules.name: The One Width Rule
rules.body: Every border in the system is `1px`. A design that seems to need a thicker line needs a different colour, a surface change, or a shadow.

rules.name: The Emphasis Is Colour Rule
rules.body: When a bordered element must feel heavier than its neighbours, darken the border. Thickness is not an available axis, because sub-pixel widths do not render consistently across displays.

rules.name: The Hero Is Earned Rule
rules.body: The hero size is available only where both are true: the section headline is the largest type on the page, and the button is the sole action in that section. Both conditions, not either. A section with two buttons has them carry each other and stays at default; a large button in a section with ordinary headings is just a large button.

dos: Do lead with Advisor Teal for actions, active states, links, and focus.
Do use Mesa Copper as restrained warmth in labels and secondary details.
Do honor each neutral section's explicit white or cream background setting.
Do use Source Serif 4 for editorial authority and Archivo for clarity and task completion.
Do build trust with real people, evidence, education, and verified claims.
Do meet WCAG 2.2 AA, including keyboard, focus, contrast, zoom, reduced motion, media, and responsive behavior.
donts: Don't copy the prototypes' exported copper default into primary actions; translate those accents to Advisor Teal unless the detail is intentionally secondary.
Don't propagate generic template colors, typography, or component treatments into canonical sections.
Don't treat migrated legacy sections as design-system authority.
Don't make the interface feel like generic SaaS, cold institutional banking, luxury-mortgage advertising, or Jimmy's national veteran-first brand.
Don't use strong shadows, pills, oversized radii, or motion as universal decoration.
Don't add the neutral background toggle to a section whose designed background should not be editor-controlled.
